log: COMPOSITION: LLM PROPOSES TEN, ESM RE-RANKS
Measured BEFORE running, and both bound the result:
* the LLM's ten are 4.8x more family-concentrated than random decoys (largest-family share
0.48 vs 0.10), so ESM faces far harder negatives than the 0.682 was scored against;
* only 3 of 2,231 protein-substrate reactions have a catalyst under 20 papers, so the obscure
stratum that forecasts orphan work does not exist here. Nothing below is an orphan number.

READING
best ESM arm 'fusion_hardneg' 0.643 vs the LLM's own ordering 0.675  (-0.032)
ceiling if a re-ranker were perfect: 0.920
REPLACING the LLM ordering: 0.141. FUSING with it (rank prior + ESM): 0.643. LLM alone: 0.675.
NO GAIN. Fusion recovers almost all of what replacement threw away, which shows the loss
was mostly discarding the LLM's ordering rather than ESM being actively wrong -- but it
still does not beat leaving the shortlist alone. ESM's 0.682 was earned against decoys
drawn at random from the whole vocabulary; the LLM's ten are 4.8x more family-concentrated,
and within one family the sequence model has nothing left to say. Telling ALDH1A1 from
ALDH3A2 is the hard problem, and it is precisely the one the composition needed solved.
NOTE the replacement arms (0.141) fall BELOW random re-ranking (0.195), and below the untrained twin (0.210).
Training made it worse on this distribution, so the coarse enzyme/substrate compatibility it
learned is mildly ANTI-correlated with which family member is right. That is a sharper
negative than noise would give, and it is the thing to explain before trying this again.
For scale, random_rerank is 0.195 -- a re-ranker that knows
nothing does not leave a good ordering alone, it flattens it to chance-within-the-list.
